differences.what: the east range's frontispiece over its side door (T-3110): the print's stone frontispiece between pilaster strips from grade (x 345-398 px) carries a small round-arched light filled with an ornamental grille (x 362-382, y 1045-1070, about 2.4-3.1 m), a paired light in the upper storey (x 355-385, y 940-985, about 4.7-5.9 m) and, through the eave, a coped gable between pinnacles with a finial (apex x 372, y 835, about 8.65 m); the build's range wall ran plain under its hip with two rows of reconstructed sash. Built (bays.p_door): 3.0 m wide, 0.1 m proud, the grilled round-headed light and the mullioned pair on its axis, a coped gable of pitch 1.5 between pinnacles; its lights render within about 5 px of the print's rows

the frontispiece's place along the range: its axis renders at x 394 against the print's 373, about 1.15 m west, because r3b's 18th Street wall (u -8.5 to -4.6, the 1911 sheet's rectangle) holds it; the print's frontispiece straddles the sheet's junction of r3b and r2, which nothing on the print marks. A K08 bay stands on one wing's wall, so moving it onto the print's axis means re-cutting the wings or carrying a bay across a junction

the side door under the frontispiece's round-arched light: a narrow door at the walk (x 368-382, y 1092-1170, its head about 1.8 m) with a glazed panel; the build has none there (no K01 wing or K08 bay cuts a door)

the east range's openings: the print's 18th Street face is blank ashlar between pilaster strips and string courses, with one column of lights a storey at x 283-300 (u about -12.6), the frontispiece's lights and nothing else between the turret and the gabled section; the build had three columns of sash on r2 and one on r3b. r2 now carries the one column at s 5.3 and r3b's light is taken out (the frontispiece stands there)

a hooded slate dormer on the east range's roof between the turret and the frontispiece (x 300-345, y 870-950, its stone face under it to about y 990): the build's wing hip carries no dormer (a K01 wing's roof takes none)
a tall stack rising behind the frontispiece's gable (x 337-403 px, its cap at about y 780, about 10 m): the build has no stack over the east range (a K01 stack stands only in the main block's roof)
the east range's eaves: about 5.9 m at the turret end through this camera against the build's 6.35 m, which T-3076 read off the Taylor print at 6.2-6.4 m; the two pictures disagree by about 0.4 m
the east range's roof: the print's slate face rises steeply from the eave to about y 800 (about 9.6-10 m) over the frontispiece; the build's 45-degree hip rises to the same line from this eye

the north-east turret: the print's cone stops in a truncated neck at about 9.6 m with no finial (y 843), the build's runs to a point about 10.1 m and a finial to 11 m; the Taylor print of c. 1895 shows the finial, so the 1965 top is a later loss

the gabled section's 18th Street face: the print's round oriel, two storeys on corbels (x 430-505 px, y 780-1000) under a balustraded balcony with an open loggia behind it, three round-arched lights under it (x 436-539, y 1020-1065) and the coped gable over (apex x 497); the build's p_gable is a flat pavilion with transomed pairs. The Taylor print's match record carries the same difference (open there)

the flank section's top: the print's third storey of paired lights under a cornice, a gabled wall dormer with a fan (sunburst) panel and a finial (x 700-800, y 400-520) and the corbel table under them (x 630-900, y 650-700); the build carries the section's wall up under K08's low hip. The Taylor print's match record carries the same difference

the main block's flank stack: the print's square stack with its heavy cap stands at x 611 (its cap at y 490), about 90 px (about 3 m) east of where the build's (u 5.0) renders; the Taylor print also puts it about 2-2.5 m east of the build's

the round tower: the print's cone is broader and lower than the build's (its eave about y 520 across x 765-1005, its finial's tip at y 183), where the build's narrow cone rises far over it; and its axis renders about 37 px west of the print's (the Taylor print holds it within 16 px). The Taylor match record's open 'tower's form' item

the loggia's carving, the front's bow and pavilion, the mansard's faces, hooded dormers and cresting, and the corner's arches: read here at the angle the Taylor print reads them, and no difference beyond its match record's
colour: the stone's tone and the slate's, in a monochrome print
the rear (east) wall, the court side and the south wall: this camera cannot see them
1965 fabric: the window air-conditioners, the iron fence, the pole, the hydrant and the lamp; not 1904 and not built

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153).
